knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5)
library(nlmixr2lib)

library(dplyr)

# Models and source

Wang 2023 relates polymyxin B exposure to acute kidney injury (AKI) in 55
critically ill adults treated in one intensive care unit. Each patient had three
steady-state polymyxin B concentrations measured (trough, mid-dosing interval
and peak), and the paper fits two logistic regressions for AKI. Both are
packaged:

1. **`Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki`** -- the final multivariable model (Equation 4):
   baseline white blood cell count (`WBC`) plus the steady-state AUC0-24 that
   the paper estimates from the peak and mid-interval concentrations
   (`AUC_POLYMYXINB`).
2. **`Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki_cmid`** -- the univariate model on the
   mid-dosing-interval concentration alone (Equation 5, `CMID_INTERVAL`),
   which the paper proposes for when only one sample can be taken.

The paper develops no population PK model. To show how the exposure inputs
can be generated, the vignette also uses `Wang_2020_polymyxinB`, a published
two-compartment population PK model for polymyxin B in Chinese adults with
multidrug-resistant Gram-negative infections. It comes from an earlier study
that Wang 2023 cites in its Introduction (reference 15).

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/psp4.13040>
* PubMed Central open access: <https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10725268/>

```{r load-models}
mod_aki <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki"))
mod_cmid <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki_cmid"))
mod_pk <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2020_polymyxinB"))
```

# Population

Wang 2023 enrolled 90 patients at Nanjing Drum Tower Hospital (August 2020 to
July 2022) and excluded 35, mostly for renal replacement therapy or a baseline
serum creatinine above 1.5 mg/dL. The 55 analysed patients (Table 1) were 64%
male, with a mean age of 61.0 years and a median weight of 62 kg; APACHE II was
20.6 +/- 5.8 and SOFA 6.3 +/- 3.0. *Acinetobacter baumannii* (69.1%) and
*Klebsiella pneumoniae* (40.0%) were the main pathogens, and the lung was the
main infection site (69.1%). The daily maintenance dose, given as two
q12h infusions, was mostly 150 mg (70.9%) or 100 mg (27.3%). Most infusions ran
over 1 h (87.3%). Concentrations were taken
after at least 48 h of therapy: the trough before a dose, the mid-dosing-interval
concentration (C1/2t) 6 h after administration, and the peak at the end of the
infusion. AKI was defined by KDIGO criteria. It occurred in 30 patients (54.5%),
between day 3 and day 17 of treatment.

```{r population, eval = FALSE}
str(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki"))
```

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Multivariable AKI model | `logit(p) = -4.623 + 0.116 * WBC + 0.040 * AUC` | Wang 2023 Equation 4 |
| `logit_ref` (`_aki`) | -4.623 | Equation 4 |
| `e_wbc_logit` | 0.116 per 10^9/L (OR 1.123, 95% CI 1.000-1.260) | Equation 4; Table 2 |
| `e_auc_logit` | 0.040 per ug*h/mL (OR 1.040, 95% CI 1.013-1.068) | Equation 4; Table 2 |
| Univariate AKI model | `logit(p) = -2.742 + 0.845 * C1/2t` | Wang 2023 Equation 5 |
| `logit_ref` (`_aki_cmid`) | -2.742 | Equation 5 |
| `e_cmid_logit` | 0.845 per ug/mL | Equation 5 |
| AUC estimator for `AUC_POLYMYXINB` | `Ke = ln(C1/C2)/t`; `AUC = t'(Ceoi + Ct)/2 + (Ceoi - Ct)/Ke` | Equations 2-3 (after Pai 2014) |
| `addSd_prob_aki` | fixed 0.001 | Not from source (Bernoulli likelihood); see Assumptions |
| Observed group summaries used below | WBC, C1/2t, AUC, Cmax, Cmin by AKI status | Table 1 |
| Discrimination | AUROC 0.805 (Eq 4), 0.747 (C1/2t) | Results, Figure 3 |

A logistic refit of the deposited patient-level dataset (Wang 2023 Data S1, 55
patients, 30 with AKI) by the maintainers returned an intercept of -4.6234 and
slopes of 0.1157 (WBC) and 0.0396 (AUC) for Equation 4, and -2.7420 and 0.8450
for Equation 5, with areas under the ROC curve of 0.805 and 0.747. These match
the published values to the printed precision.

# Check 1 -- the printed equations and their published landmarks

Each model is evaluated once per subject: there are no dose events and no time
dimension, so a one-row data frame per covariate combination is enough.

```{r helpers}
# The models have no random effects, so rxode2 notes that a multi-subject
# simulation has no omega; that note is expected here and is muffled.
muffle_no_omega <- function(w) {
  if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
    invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
}
prob_aki <- function(mod, covs) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = seq_len(nrow(covs)), time = 0, evid = 0L, covs)
  sim <- withCallingHandlers(
    rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = ev, returnType = "data.frame"),
    warning = muffle_no_omega
  )
  as.data.frame(sim)$prob_aki
}
```

```{r check-landmarks}
theta_aki <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki"))$theta
theta_cmid <- rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2023_polymyxinB_aki_cmid"))$theta

landmarks <- c(
  or_wbc = exp(theta_aki[["e_wbc_logit"]]),
  or_auc = exp(theta_aki[["e_auc_logit"]]),
  cmid_at_p50 = -theta_cmid[["logit_ref"]] / theta_cmid[["e_cmid_logit"]],
  p_at_3.24 = prob_aki(mod_cmid, data.frame(CMID_INTERVAL = 3.24))
)
round(landmarks, 4)

stopifnot(
  # Table 2 odds ratios, to the printed 3 decimals (0.04 is printed to 2
  # significant figures in Equation 4, so its OR is 1.041 against 1.040).
  abs(landmarks[["or_wbc"]] - 1.123) < 0.001,
  abs(landmarks[["or_auc"]] - 1.040) < 0.002,
  # Results: "The probability of AKI was >50% when C1/2t was >=3.24".
  abs(landmarks[["cmid_at_p50"]] - 3.24) < 0.01,
  abs(landmarks[["p_at_3.24"]] - 0.5) < 0.005
)
```

# Check 2 -- predicted AKI incidence in a cohort built from Table 1

A logistic regression reproduces the observed event rate of the data it was fitted
to. The patient-level data are not reproduced here, so the vignette builds each
Table 1 group (25 without and 30 with AKI) deterministically from the published
group summaries:

* WBC is log-normal, matched to the group median and interquartile range.
* AUC and C1/2t are normal, matched to the group mean and SD.

WBC and AUC are crossed independently; in the deposited data their correlation
is 0.03. The quantile grid uses no random numbers, so the result is identical on
every machine.

```{r cohort}
q <- stats::ppoints(25)
table1 <- tibble::tribble(
  ~group,    ~n, ~wbc_med, ~wbc_q1, ~wbc_q3, ~auc_mean, ~auc_sd, ~cmid_mean, ~cmid_sd,
  "non-AKI", 25, 8.5,      5.8,     11.3,    77.7,      21.8,    3.0,        0.9,
  "AKI",     30, 10.8,     8.1,     17.2,    103.7,     31.2,    4.1,        1.3
)

group_prob <- function(row) {
  wbc <- exp(log(row$wbc_med) + stats::qnorm(q) *
    (log(row$wbc_q3) - log(row$wbc_q1)) / (2 * stats::qnorm(0.75)))
  auc <- row$auc_mean + stats::qnorm(q) * row$auc_sd
  cmid <- row$cmid_mean + stats::qnorm(q) * row$cmid_sd
  grid <- expand.grid(WBC = wbc, AUC_POLYMYXINB = auc)
  tibble::tibble(
    group = row$group, n = row$n,
    p_eq4 = mean(prob_aki(mod_aki, grid)),
    p_eq5 = mean(prob_aki(mod_cmid, data.frame(CMID_INTERVAL = cmid)))
  )
}

cohort_prob <- dplyr::bind_rows(lapply(split(table1, table1$group), group_prob))
overall <- cohort_prob |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    group = "overall",
    p_eq4 = sum(n * p_eq4) / sum(n), p_eq5 = sum(n * p_eq5) / sum(n),
    n = sum(n)
  )
cohort_tbl <- dplyr::bind_rows(cohort_prob, overall) |>
  dplyr::mutate(observed = c(AKI = 1, `non-AKI` = 0, overall = 30 / 55)[group])

cohort_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Group" = group, "N" = n, "Mean P(AKI), Equation 4" = p_eq4,
    "Mean P(AKI), Equation 5" = p_eq5, "Observed AKI fraction" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Mean model-predicted AKI probability in cohorts reconstructed from Wang 2023 Table 1.")

stopifnot(
  # Deterministic. Realised 0.551 (Eq 4) and 0.556 (Eq 5) against 30/55 =
  # 0.545. A mis-signed slope or a 10-fold unit slip on WBC, AUC or C1/2t
  # moves the overall rate by far more than 0.05.
  abs(overall$p_eq4 - 30 / 55) < 0.05,
  abs(overall$p_eq5 - 30 / 55) < 0.05,
  # Both models must rank the AKI group above the non-AKI group.
  cohort_prob$p_eq4[cohort_prob$group == "AKI"] > cohort_prob$p_eq4[cohort_prob$group == "non-AKI"],
  cohort_prob$p_eq5[cohort_prob$group == "AKI"] > cohort_prob$p_eq5[cohort_prob$group == "non-AKI"]
)
```

# Figure 4 -- probability of AKI against the mid-dosing-interval concentration

```{r figure-4, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 4 of Wang 2023."}
cmid_grid <- seq(0, 8, by = 0.05)
fig4 <- tibble::tibble(
  cmid = cmid_grid,
  prob = prob_aki(mod_cmid, data.frame(CMID_INTERVAL = cmid_grid))
)

ggplot(fig4, aes(cmid, prob)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 3.47, linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.5, linetype = "dotted") +
  annotate("rect", xmin = 1.438, xmax = 7.030, ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, alpha = 0.08) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Polymyxin B mid-dosing-interval concentration C1/2t (ug/mL)",
    y = "P(acute kidney injury)",
    caption = paste(
      "Replicates Figure 4 of Wang 2023. Dashed: ROC cutoff 3.47 ug/mL;",
      "shaded: observed C1/2t range 1.438-7.030 ug/mL."
    )
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Figure -- multivariable model surface

The paper does not plot Equation 4. The figure shows its predicted probability
across the observed AUC range at the Table 1 WBC quartiles. The paper's
cutoff of 0.57 on this probability gave 70% sensitivity and 80% specificity.

```{r figure-eq4, fig.cap = "Equation 4 of Wang 2023 at the cohort WBC quartiles."}
eq4_grid <- expand.grid(WBC = c(7.3, 9.6, 13.4), AUC_POLYMYXINB = seq(30, 180, by = 1))
eq4_grid$prob <- prob_aki(mod_aki, eq4_grid)

ggplot(eq4_grid, aes(AUC_POLYMYXINB, prob, colour = factor(WBC))) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.57, linetype = "dashed") +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1)) +
  labs(
    x = "Polymyxin B AUC0-24 by the first-order equation (ug*h/mL)",
    y = "P(acute kidney injury)", colour = "WBC (10^9/L)",
    caption = "Dashed: the paper's Youden-optimal cutoff 0.57 on the predicted probability."
  ) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Generating the exposure inputs from a population PK model

In clinical use, the AUC and the mid-interval concentration come from therapeutic
drug monitoring samples. To show the full chain, this section simulates
steady-state polymyxin B profiles with `Wang_2020_polymyxinB`. It then derives
the three Wang 2023 exposure metrics from those profiles and passes them to both
AKI models.

## Virtual cohort and simulation

The cohort has two maintenance-dose arms of 100 subjects each: 100 mg/day and
150 mg/day, given as 50 mg and 75 mg every 12 h and infused over 1 h. Together
these cover 98% of the Wang 2023 patients. Table 1 tabulates the maintenance
dose per day; the Methods give it as 2.5-3 mg/kg/day in two divided doses. Creatinine clearance, the only covariate of the PK model, is
log-normal and matched to the Table 1 mean +/- SD of 129.6 +/- 62.8 mL/min.
Baseline WBC is log-normal and matched to the overall Table 1 median (IQR) of
9.6 (7.3, 13.4) x 10^9/L. Ten doses are given. The 24 h after the 9th dose
(96-120 h, the fifth day) are sampled densely, so PKNCA sees a full steady-state
day.

```{r pk-cohort}
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20231)
n_per_arm <- 100
crcl_sdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (62.8 / 129.6)^2))
wbc_sdlog <- (log(13.4) - log(7.3)) / (2 * stats::qnorm(0.75))

subjects <- tibble::tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_per_arm),
  daily_dose = rep(c(100, 150), each = n_per_arm),
  dose = daily_dose / 2,
  CRCL = exp(stats::rnorm(2 * n_per_arm, log(129.6) - crcl_sdlog^2 / 2, crcl_sdlog)),
  WBC = exp(stats::rnorm(2 * n_per_arm, log(9.6), wbc_sdlog))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = paste(daily_dose, "mg/day"))

dose_times <- seq(0, 108, by = 12)
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(96, 120, by = 0.25), 97, 102, 109, 114)))

dose_rows <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = dose_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = dose, rate = dose / 1, evid = 1L, cmt = "central")
obs_rows <- subjects |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(dose_rows, obs_rows) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, rate, evid, cmt, CRCL)
```

```{r pk-simulate}
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_pk, events = events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  as.data.frame() |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(subjects, id, treatment, dose, WBC), by = "id")
```

## PKNCA over the steady-state day

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc), time >= 96) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, Cc) |>
  dplyr::distinct(id, time, .keep_all = TRUE)
dose_df <- dplyr::filter(dose_rows, time >= 96, time < 120) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, time, amt)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = 96, end = 120, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE)
nca <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_wide <- as.data.frame(nca$result) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)
```

## The Wang 2023 exposure metrics from the simulated samples

The three TDM samples are read off the simulated profile at the Wang 2023
landmarks for a 1-h infusion of the dose at 108 h: the peak at 109 h (end of
infusion), C1/2t at 114 h (6 h after the start of the dose) and the trough at
120 h. The AUC is then estimated from the peak and C1/2t by Equations 2-3. The
time between the two samples is 5 h; this spacing reproduces the AUC values in
the deposited dataset.

```{r pai}
# Wang 2023 Equations 2-3 (after Pai 2014): one-compartment first-order
# estimate of the AUC over one dosing interval from two steady-state samples,
# scaled from the 12-h interval to 24 h.
auc_pai_0_24 <- function(cmax, cmid, tinf = 1, tau = 12, dt = 5) {
  ke <- log(cmax / cmid) / dt
  ctrough <- cmax * exp(-ke * (tau - tinf))
  (24 / tau) * (tinf * (cmax + ctrough) / 2 + (cmax - ctrough) / ke)
}

# Known-answer check of the estimator: for a mono-exponential profile after an
# (almost) instantaneous input it is exact, AUC0-tau = C0 * (1 - exp(-k tau)) / k.
k_test <- 0.12
c0_test <- 8
auc_true <- 2 * c0_test * (1 - exp(-k_test * 12)) / k_test
auc_est <- auc_pai_0_24(c0_test, c0_test * exp(-5 * k_test), tinf = 1e-6)
stopifnot(abs(auc_est / auc_true - 1) < 1e-5)

tdm <- sim |>
  dplyr::filter(time %in% c(109, 114, 120)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, treatment, dose, WBC, time, Cc) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = time, values_from = Cc, names_prefix = "c") |>
  dplyr::rename(cmax_tdm = c109, cmid = c114, cmin_tdm = c120) |>
  dplyr::mutate(auc_pai = auc_pai_0_24(cmax_tdm, cmid)) |>
  dplyr::left_join(dplyr::select(nca_wide, id, auclast), by = "id")

pai_ratio <- tdm$auc_pai / tdm$auclast
round(stats::quantile(pai_ratio, c(0.05, 0.5, 0.95)), 3)

stopifnot(
  # The one-compartment two-sample estimate tracks the dense-grid PKNCA AUC of
  # the two-compartment profile closely: by 5 h after the infusion the
  # distribution phase is largely over. The tail quantile is robust to which
  # subjects draw an extreme Q.
  abs(stats::median(pai_ratio) - 1) < 0.10,
  stats::quantile(abs(pai_ratio - 1), 0.9) < 0.25
)
```

## Comparison against the Wang 2023 concentrations

Table 1 reports the observed cohort means. The simulated means are weighted by
the Wang 2023 split of daily maintenance doses: 15 patients on 100 mg/day and
39 on 150 mg/day. The one patient on 200 mg/day is not represented.

```{r nca-compare}
w <- c(`100 mg/day` = 15, `150 mg/day` = 39)
sim_means <- nca_wide |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmax, cmin, auclast), mean)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmax, cmin, auclast), ~ sum(.x * w[treatment]) / sum(w)))

reference <- data.frame(cmax = 7.5, cmin = 2.2, auclast = 99.1)

cmp <- nlmixr2lib::ncaComparisonTable(
  simulated = sim_means,
  reference = reference,
  units = c(cmax = "ug/mL", cmin = "ug/mL", auclast = "ug*h/mL, 0-24 h"),
  tolerance_pct = 20
)
knitr::kable(
  cmp,
  digits = 2,
  caption = paste(
    "Dose-weighted mean steady-state NCA from Wang_2020_polymyxinB against the",
    "Wang 2023 Table 1 cohort means. The reference AUC is the three-sample",
    "trapezoidal AUC0-24 (Cmin, C1/2t, Cmax); the simulated AUC uses the full",
    "simulated grid. * differs by more than 20%."
  )
)

derived <- tdm |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(cmid = mean(cmid), auc_pai = mean(auc_pai)) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmid, auc_pai), ~ sum(.x * w[treatment]) / sum(w)))
derived_tbl <- tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("C1/2t (ug/mL)", "AUC0-24 by Equations 2-3 (ug*h/mL)"),
  reference = c(3.6, 91.9),
  simulated = c(derived$cmid, derived$auc_pai)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (simulated / reference - 1))
derived_tbl |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Exposure metric" = metric, "Wang 2023 Table 1 mean" = reference,
    "Simulated (dose-weighted mean)" = simulated, "% diff" = pct_diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "The two exposure inputs of the AKI models: simulated against Wang 2023 Table 1.")
```

`r sprintf("The simulated dose-weighted means differ from the Wang 2023 Table 1 means by %.0f%% (Cmax), %.0f%% (Cmin), %.0f%% (C1/2t) and %.0f%% (AUC by Equations 2-3).", 100 * (sim_means$cmax / 7.5 - 1), 100 * (sim_means$cmin / 2.2 - 1), 100 * (derived$cmid / 3.6 - 1), 100 * (derived$auc_pai / 91.9 - 1))`
The PK model was developed in a different cohort, in patients sampled on day 4,
so the agreement is a plausibility check of the chain, not a validation of the
AKI models.

## Predicted AKI risk by maintenance dose

```{r risk-by-dose}
tdm$p_eq4 <- prob_aki(mod_aki, data.frame(WBC = tdm$WBC, AUC_POLYMYXINB = tdm$auc_pai))
tdm$p_eq5 <- prob_aki(mod_cmid, data.frame(CMID_INTERVAL = tdm$cmid))

risk <- tdm |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median_auc = stats::median(auc_pai), median_cmid = stats::median(cmid),
    mean_p_eq4 = mean(p_eq4), mean_p_eq5 = mean(p_eq5)
  ) |>
  dplyr::mutate(observed = c(4 / 15, 25 / 39))

risk |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Daily maintenance dose" = treatment, "Median AUC0-24 (ug*h/mL)" = median_auc,
    "Median C1/2t (ug/mL)" = median_cmid, "Mean P(AKI), Equation 4" = mean_p_eq4,
    "Mean P(AKI), Equation 5" = mean_p_eq5, "Observed AKI fraction (Table 1)" = observed
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 3, caption = "Simulated exposure and predicted AKI risk by maintenance dose; observed fractions are 4/15 and 25/39 from Wang 2023 Table 1.")

stopifnot(
  # Both models are monotone in exposure, and 150 mg/day gives 1.5-fold the
  # exposure of 100 mg/day in a linear PK model, so the higher dose must carry the
  # higher mean risk whatever cohort is drawn.
  risk$mean_p_eq4[2] > risk$mean_p_eq4[1],
  risk$mean_p_eq5[2] > risk$mean_p_eq5[1]
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **No residual error and no random effects in the source.** Both regressions
  have a Bernoulli likelihood. The fixed additive residual
  `addSd_prob_aki = 0.001` is not a published quantity; it only gives rxode2
  an error model to attach to the probability. Use the `prob_aki` column, not
  a simulated observation, as the model prediction.
* **AUC estimator.** `AUC_POLYMYXINB` is the quantity the regression was fitted
  to: an AUC0-24 from the peak and C1/2t by the one-compartment first-order
  equation. Wang 2023 states only that C1/2t was drawn "6 h after
  administration". The maintainers found that the AUC values in the deposited
  dataset are reproduced to within 1.0% when the two samples are taken 5 h
  apart for every patient, including the seven infused over 2 or 2.5 h. The
  `auc_pai_0_24()` helper above uses that convention. An AUC0-24 from a
  population PK model can be supplied instead; the simulation above shows the
  two agree closely for this drug.
* **Landmark.** Both models are static and the probability applies to the whole
  treatment course. AKI was observed between day 3 and day 17. The paper gives
  no time course of risk, and the models carry none.
* **Variables screened but not retained.** Maintenance dose, neutrophil
  percentage, Cmin, Cmax, C1/2t and the AUCs estimated by the other methods
  were all significant in univariate analysis. Forward stepwise selection kept
  only WBC and the C1/2t-Cmax AUC. These variables are listed under
  `covariatesDataExcluded`; no coefficients are published for them.
* **Female percentage.** Table 1 prints "30 (36.7)" for female patients, which
  conflicts with 35 male patients out of 55. The non-AKI and AKI columns (12 and
  8) sum to 20, so `sex_female_pct` is recorded as 20/55 = 36.4%.
* **PK chain.** The population PK model is `Wang_2020_polymyxinB`, not a model
  from this paper. Its cohort, creatinine-clearance distribution and day-4
  sampling differ from the Wang 2023 cohort. The comparison tables check the
  chain for plausibility only. The 1-h infusion and the two-arm dose split are
  simplifications of the Wang 2023 regimens.
